assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues redefined what a small molecule can do: instead of occupying an active site it recruits an E3 ligase to destroy a target, reaching proteins once thought undruggable. It is a clear molecular design principle with immediate consequences for chemical biology and clinical translation, which is the kind of discovery that changes what researchers and clinicians can actually do.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced and developed the PROTAC concept, while Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains the molecular glue branch. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made major contributions, so a three-person limit leaves real credit questions.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials and the mechanism is reproduced across many labs and E3 ligases. Clinical approval is still limited, but the chemistry is firmly established, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should split PROTAC design from the cereblon molecular-glue discovery is unresolved.
No PROTAC has yet reached approval as far as I know, so clinical validation is incomplete (not independently verified).
Credit is spread across many contributors (Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito, Kim).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry that made siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines deliverable, tying lipid pKa and self-assembly to endosomal escape and to real patient benefit. The scientific and societal impact is very large and easy to explain.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the lipid nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid principles with Hope, Madden and MacLachlan, while Anderson and Langer drove combinatorial lipid discovery. The group is large and the share of credit among them is contested; I would centre on Cullis as the main architect with Anderson.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is established at scale by the siRNA drug Onpattro and by the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, so the technology is mature. Because the 2023 Medicine prize honored nucleoside-modified mRNA, a Chemistry prize on the delivery side would be complementary.
uncertainties: Attribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is difficult.
Patent and priority disputes may complicate the record (not verified).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing is a chemistry-driven tool that converts one base into another by deaminase chemistry without double-strand breaks, giving precise genome editing with therapeutic promise. It combines protein engineering, evolved enzymes and nucleoside chemistry, and it opened a clinical path for point-mutation diseases.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the intellectual driver, with Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors) as lead developers. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase-based approach, so priority is not entirely clean. Prime editing (B049) is a related Liu contribution that could be recognized together or separately.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication is extensive and the first clinical data are encouraging. The 2020 Chemistry prize already honored CRISPR-Cas9, so timing and overlap with that prize are a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a Liu-only prize covering base and prime editing is open.
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy remain to be shown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically encoding noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs gives chemists site-specific control over protein composition in living cells. The method is a general molecular design tool used for probes, crosslinkers, photocaged residues and engineered biologics, and it spread widely across biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair strategy and the first expansion in E. coli and yeast, Wang was central in the early work, and Chin extended it to eukaryotes and to reassigned codons and genomically recoded organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed, so some credit is left out.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent use confirm its robustness. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Priority among the Schultz lab alumni and the Chin lab work needs careful weighing.
The balance between early foundational and later expansion work (quadruplet codons, ribosome engineering) is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed assembly of gold nanoparticles established a rational route to colloidal crystals and yielded spherical nucleic acids that enter cells, with direct impact on nanoplasmonic detection assays, diagnostics and gene regulation. This is close to my own field, where recognition-driven nanoparticle assembly gave bioanalytical chemistry new capabilities.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos published the founding 1996 papers and Mirkin developed spherical nucleic acids, so a two-person configuration seems fair. Storhoff and Mucic were students or postdocs, and the narrower credited set is plausible.
assessment.maturity: The concept is broadly replicated and commercial diagnostics exist, but clinical therapeutic use of spherical nucleic acids is still emerging.
uncertainties: The biomedical therapeutic impact is less proven than the assembly and sensing impact.
Alivisatos is also credited in the quantum dot area, which was recognized in 2023, so overlap may count against him (not verified).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read out enzyme function, rather than abundance, in complex proteomes. It brought a chemical logic into functional proteomics, enabled inhibitor discovery in native systems and is now a standard approach in drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the main figure, with Bogyo and Overkleeft as major developers of probe chemistries for protease classes. Weerapana was a key co-developer of cysteine reactivity profiling, so credit extends beyond three people.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted over almost thirty years and used in clinical-stage programs, so the method is well established.
uncertainties: The relative weight of Cravatt versus the probe-design contributions of others is unclear.
It may be seen as an enabling toolbox rather than one decisive discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket cracked a target long deemed undruggable and led to approved drugs, and his earlier analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics gave a general way to dissect kinase signaling. The work shows how precise chemical design translates into therapy.
assessment.attribution: The credit is a single name, which keeps attribution simple, although later drug development by companies (Amgen, Mirati) is a separate effort and the KRAS inhibitor discoveries involved many groups.
assessment.maturity: Clinical approvals of sotorasib and adagrasib confirm the concept, but the story is still evolving with resistance mechanisms and the broader RAS inhibitor field.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a single decisive discovery or two separate achievements (KRAS and chemical genetics).
Contributions from industry teams may complicate a Shokat-only award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides and clustered amplification on a surface transformed biology and medicine, with chemistry at its core. Its scale of impact is hard to overstate, and the underlying nucleotide chemistry is a molecular design success.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry; Ju and Mayer contributed related reversible terminator and clustering ideas, and Rothberg's pyrosequencing platform is distinct, so a two-person prize is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: The technology has dominated sequencing for fifteen years and is thoroughly validated, so recognition is more than ripe.
uncertainties: Priority claims among Solexa, Ju (Columbia) and Mayer (Manteia) must be weighed.
Sequencing may be viewed as primarily a biological or engineering success rather than chemistry (not verified).
